solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/angle-between-hands-of-a-clock/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

1344. Angle Between Hands of a Clock

Given two numbers, hour and minutes, return the smaller angle (in degrees) formed between the hour and the minute hand.

Answers within 10^-5 of the actual value will be accepted as correct.

Example 1:

Input: hour = 12, minutes = 30
Output: 165

Example 2:

Input: hour = 3, minutes = 30
Output: 75

Example 3:

Input: hour = 3, minutes = 15
Output: 7.5

Constraints:

    1 <= hour <= 12
    0 <= minutes <= 59
"""


class Solution:
    def angleClock(self, hour: int, minutes: int) -> float:
        # Calculate the angle of the hour hand
        hour_angle = (hour % 12) * 30 + (minutes * 0.5)
        # Calculate the angle of the minute hand
        minute_angle = minutes * 6
        # Calculate the difference
        diff = abs(hour_angle - minute_angle)
        # Return the smaller angle
        return min(diff, 360 - diff)


sol = Solution()

print(sol.angleClock(12, 30))  # 165

assert abs(sol.angleClock(12, 30) - 165) < 1e-5
assert abs(sol.angleClock(3, 30) - 75) < 1e-5
assert abs(sol.angleClock(3, 15) - 7.5) < 1e-5

assert sol.angleClock(12, 0) == 0.0
assert sol.angleClock(1, 0) == 30.0
assert sol.angleClock(6, 0) == 180.0
assert sol.angleClock(12, 59) == 35.5
assert sol.angleClock(11, 59) == 5.5
assert sol.angleClock(6, 30) == 15.0
assert sol.angleClock(9, 45) == 22.5
assert sol.angleClock(3, 0) == 90.0
assert sol.angleClock(12, 15) == 82.5
assert sol.angleClock(10, 10) == 115.0
assert sol.angleClock(5, 55) == 152.5
assert sol.angleClock(7, 29) == 50.5
